nodes.name: .gitattributes
nodes.summary: Git line-ending and binary-file rules for the project, marking .gd and shell scripts as LF text and .xcf/.png assets as binary to prevent corruption during cross-platform checkout.

nodes.name: holloway_four_winds_act1.yarn
nodes.summary: YarnSpinner dialogue node for Holloway's Act 1 conversation at the Four Winds bar; uses the $intro_complete variable to branch between two beats — a dismissive warning to a newcomer or a quiet solitary greeting.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a YarnSpinner <<if>>/<</endif>> block to conditionally display different dialogue lines based on the $intro_complete game variable, illustrating state-aware branching.

nodes.name: iris_intro.yarn
nodes.summary: YarnSpinner dialogue node for Iris's introduction scene; presents Reid with two player-choice options ('I'm detecting' / 'I'm building suspense'), each leading into a short banter exchange that characterizes Iris as dry and impatient.
nodes.languageNotes: Demonstrates YarnSpinner shortcut options (-> syntax) for player choices within a single node, without branching to separate named nodes.

nodes.name: iris.yarnproject
nodes.summary: YarnSpinner project manifest referencing all *.yarn dialogue scripts in the project; compiled by the C# YarnSpinner importer into a .tres resource loaded at runtime via the GDScript/C# bridge.
nodes.languageNotes: The sourceFiles glob '**/*.yarn' means any newly added .yarn file is automatically included in the compiled dialogue project without modifying this file.

nodes.name: project.godot
nodes.summary: Master Godot 4.6 project configuration registering all autoloads (SceneManager, DialogueManager, GameState, etc.), setting the 320x180 canvas resolution upscaled to 1280x720, enabling the C#/Mobile feature set, and mapping keyboard input actions for movement and interaction.
nodes.languageNotes: Registers DialogueManager as a scene-based autoload (scenes/autoload/DialogueManager.tscn), which is important because it carries a full scene tree with the DialogueRunner, YarnDialogueBridge, and GameStateVariableStorage child nodes.

nodes.name: DialogueManager.tscn
nodes.summary: Autoload scene that wires together the entire dialogue pipeline: a YarnSpinner C# DialogueRunner (consuming iris.yarnproject), a GDScript YarnDialogueBridge presenter, a C# GameStateVariableStorage, and the DialogueBox UI — all mounted under a CanvasLayer at layer 10.
nodes.languageNotes: Bridges C# (DialogueRunner, GameStateVariableStorage) with GDScript (yarn_dialogue_bridge.gd, dialogue_manager.gd) using Godot's node-based signal/method architecture rather than direct cross-language calls.

nodes.name: DialogueBox.tscn
nodes.summary: UI scene for the dialogue HUD panel anchored to the bottom of the viewport, containing a speaker name label, a RichTextLabel for dialogue body text with BBCode support, and a hidden VBoxContainer for player choice buttons.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses offset_top=-56 on a bottom-anchored Panel to create a fixed-height strip at the bottom of the 320x180 canvas. The ChoiceList VBoxContainer is hidden by default and shown only when player options are available.

nodes.name: NPC.tscn
nodes.summary: Base NPC scene template combining a Node2D root with npc.gd script and an offset Sprite2D, used as an instanced scene for world characters that can trigger dialogue.

nodes.name: _show_line_internal

nodes.name: run_line_async

nodes.name: run_options_async

nodes.name: start_dialogue

nodes.summary: C# DialoguePresenterBase implementation that mediates between the YarnSpinner async runner and the GDScript dialogue UI — emits Godot signals for each presentation step (line, options, complete) and exposes ContinueLine/SelectOption/StartDialogue for GDScript to call back.
nodes.name: YarnDialogueBridge.cs

nodes.summary: Godot Node subclassing YarnSpinner DialoguePresenterBase, handling async line/options/complete callbacks from the runner and exposing synchronous GDScript-callable methods for UI interaction.
nodes.name: YarnDialogueBridge

nodes.name: RunLineAsync

nodes.summary: Called by YarnSpinner when choices are available; emits a Godot signal and suspends the async task until SelectOption is called with the player chosen index.

nodes.name: YarnTaskCompletionSource<T>

nodes.name: ICommandDispatcher
nodes.summary: Interface contract for command dispatchers in YarnSpinner-Godot, requiring dispatch, project setup, and command registry access.

nodes.name: YarnActionAttribute.cs

nodes.name: YarnActionAttribute

nodes.name: YarnCommandAttribute
nodes.summary: Attribute marking a method as a YarnSpinner command with a specified command string and optional scene-injector method name.

nodes.name: YarnFunctionAttribute.cs

nodes.name: YarnFunctionAttribute

nodes.name: CustomMarker

nodes.name: DialogueRunner.cs

nodes.name: DialogueRunner

nodes.name: StartDialogue
nodes.summary: Starts dialogue from a named Yarn node: initialises cancellation tokens, loads the program, notifies all presenters via OnDialogueStartedAsync (supporting both C# and GDScript presenters), then drives the dialogue VM with Continue().

nodes.name: RunLocalisedLine
nodes.summary: Delivers a localised dialogue line to all presenter nodes asynchronously, managing per-line cancellation tokens for skip/hurry-up, dispatching to both C# async presenters and GDScript presenters via reflection.

nodes.name: OnOptionsReceivedAsync
nodes.summary: Handles an options block from the Yarn VM: localises each option, presents them to all option-aware presenters, waits for a selection (via TaskCompletionSource), then feeds the chosen option back to the VM.

nodes.name: SplitCommandText

nodes.name: FunctionInfo.cs

nodes.name: SetAllVariables

nodes.name: LanguageAttribute.cs

nodes.name: LineMetadataTableEntry

tour.title: Dialogue Content: Yarn Scripts
tour.description: Every conversation in The Hollow Men starts as a plain-text .yarn file in the dialogue/ folder. iris_intro.yarn and holloway_four_winds_act1.yarn show the two authoring patterns the project uses: player-choice branches and variable-gated conditional beats. Reading these first makes every other layer make sense — the entire runtime exists solely to execute scripts that look like these.
tour.languageLesson: YarnSpinner script files use a node/header syntax: `title: NodeName` then `---` to open the body and `===` to close it. Choices are prefixed with `->`, variables are prefixed with `$`, and `<<if $var>>` / `<<else>>` / `<<endif>>` control branching. Each .yarn file can contain many named nodes; the runner jumps between them by node title.

tour.title: The YarnProject Manifest
tour.description: iris.yarnproject is the glue between the authored scripts and the C# runtime. It is a JSON manifest that lists every *.yarn source file and is compiled by the YarnSpinner Godot importer into a binary .tres resource at import time. The DialogueRunner node references this compiled resource at startup — so adding a new .yarn file means adding it here first.
tour.languageLesson: The .yarnproject file is both a build manifest and a Godot resource. When Godot imports it, the C# YarnProjectImporter compiles all listed .yarn files into a single serialised YarnProject resource. The .tres/.md5 sidecar files this produces are gitignored — they must be regenerated after every .yarn edit by running a headless Godot import.

tour.title: Registering the System: project.godot
tour.description: Before any dialogue code runs, Godot must know the DialogueManager exists. project.godot registers DialogueManager.tscn as an autoload singleton, making it available everywhere under the name `DialogueManager`. This is also where the C# feature set and the YarnSpinner plugin are enabled — without both, the C#/GDScript bridge can't compile.
tour.languageLesson: Godot autoloads are scene or script nodes Godot instantiates before any game scene and keeps alive for the entire session. They are accessed as global names (e.g. `DialogueManager.run_node(...)`) from any GDScript without importing or requiring a node reference. An autoload backed by a .tscn scene (rather than a bare .gd) can wire together a subtree of multiple child nodes at startup.

tour.title: The Dialogue Pipeline Scene
tour.description: DialogueManager.tscn is the scene that project.godot loads as the autoload. It is the wiring diagram for the whole system: a single CanvasLayer (layer 10, always on top) whose children are the DialogueRunner C# node, the YarnDialogueBridge C# presenter, the GameStateVariableStorage C# node, and the DialogueBox UI scene. Understanding this scene's node tree answers the question 'how do all these pieces find each other at runtime?'
tour.languageLesson: Godot .tscn files are human-readable text scenes. Each [node] section declares a name, type, script, and parent path. When a C# class and a GDScript class need to cooperate, the easiest Godot pattern is to make them siblings or parent/child in the same scene — then one can call `GetNode<T>` (C#) or `get_node()` (GDScript) to reach the other without any dependency injection.

tour.title: The World Trigger: NPC Scene and Script
tour.description: Dialogue begins in the world when the player presses the interact key next to an NPC. NPC.tscn is the base scene template for all world characters; npc.gd reads its YarnSpinner node ID from Tiled tile metadata on `_ready`, registers itself with CellRegistry as an interactable, and when `interact()` is called it delegates immediately to `DialogueManager.run_node(yarn_node_id)`. This is the single entry point that kicks off the entire dialogue pipeline.
tour.languageLesson: In this project, NPC data (which dialogue node to run, display name) is stored as Tiled tile metadata rather than hardcoded in GDScript. On `_ready`, npc.gd reads `get_meta('yarn_node_id', '')` from its parent TileMapLayer cell data. This keeps the world editor (Tiled) as the single source of truth for NPC configuration — changing an NPC's dialogue requires only editing the map, not the script.

tour.title: The Public API: dialogue_manager.gd
tour.description: dialogue_manager.gd is the single surface the rest of the game touches. It exposes `run_node(node_id)` — the function npc.gd calls — plus `show_text`, `show_narration`, and `skip_or_dismiss` for non-Yarn dialogue. It also re-emits `dialogue_opened` and `dialogue_closed` signals from the underlying DialogueBox so the rest of the game can react to dialogue state changes without knowing which subsystem is driving them.
tour.languageLesson: GDScript autoload singletons are the GDScript equivalent of a service locator. Wrapping the internal YarnDialogueBridge/DialogueBox in a thin public API like dialogue_manager.gd means the NPC, the battle system, and cutscene scripts all call one consistent interface — if the underlying dialogue engine were swapped out, only dialogue_manager.gd would change.

tour.title: The C# Runner: DialogueRunner
tour.description: DialogueRunner.cs is the YarnSpinner-Godot library's core node — it loads the compiled YarnProject, walks the bytecode instruction by instruction, and dispatches each event (line, options set, command) to registered presenter nodes. When `run_node` is called, it is ultimately this C# node's `StartDialogue` that begins executing the selected .yarn node. DialogueRunner.GDScript.cs is a partial class that adds serialisation helpers, converting C# `LocalizedLine` objects into Godot Dictionary types that GDScript can read.
tour.languageLesson: C# partial classes split a single class definition across multiple files. YarnSpinner-Godot uses this to keep GDScript interop helpers (DialogueRunner.GDScript.cs) separate from core dialogue execution logic (DialogueRunner.cs). This is a clean separation of concerns: the main file stays focused on the YarnSpinner state machine while the GDScript partial handles the Godot Dictionary/Array marshalling needed to cross the C#/GDScript boundary.

tour.title: The C# Bridge: YarnDialogueBridge.cs
tour.description: YarnDialogueBridge.cs implements `DialoguePresenterBase`, which is the interface the DialogueRunner calls for every presentation event. For each line and options set, it translates the C# `LocalizedLine` / `DialogueOption[]` into a Godot-friendly form and calls the sibling GDScript node's methods (`run_line_async`, `run_options_async`) via GodotObject interop. It also exposes `ContinueLine`, `SelectOption`, and `StartDialogue` so the GDScript side can signal back when the player has responded.
tour.languageLesson: Godot's C#/GDScript interop works through the GodotObject.Call() and GodotObject.EmitSignal() APIs. A C# node can call GDScript methods by string name, and a GDScript node can call C# methods the same way. This project takes the extra step of pairing each C# bridge class with a GDScript counterpart so that the async await pattern can be used naturally on both sides without blocking Godot's main thread.

tour.title: The GDScript Bridge: yarn_dialogue_bridge.gd
tour.description: yarn_dialogue_bridge.gd is the GDScript half of the bridge pair. Its `run_line_async` and `run_options_async` methods are called directly by the C# side; they hand the line data and choices to DialogueBox, then `await` a signal (line_advanced or option_selected) before returning to C#, which in turn unblocks the YarnSpinner runner so it can move to the next instruction. This two-file bridge is the architectural seam where the async C# world and the signal-driven GDScript world meet.
tour.languageLesson: GDScript's `await signal_name` suspends the current coroutine until the signal fires, then resumes — exactly like C# `await`. When C# calls a GDScript method that internally awaits a signal, it needs to do so via a compatible async shim (YarnTask in this project) rather than a blocking C# `Task.Wait()`, which would deadlock Godot's single-threaded main loop.

tour.title: The UI Layer: DialogueBox
tour.description: DialogueBox.tscn and dialogue_box.gd implement everything the player sees: the bottom-anchored panel, speaker name label, RichTextLabel body with BBCode support, and the choice button list. The script manages three explicit states — IDLE, SHOWING_LINE, SHOWING_CHOICES — with a character-by-character typewriter effect during SHOWING_LINE. Pressing interact either skips to the end of the typewriter animation or, once complete, advances the line by emitting `line_advanced`, which unblocks yarn_dialogue_bridge.gd's await.
tour.languageLesson: The typewriter effect is implemented as a Godot Tween that increments a `visible_ratio` property on the RichTextLabel — this is Godot's built-in way to reveal BBCode text character by character without managing character indices manually. State-machine-style enum states (IDLE / SHOWING_LINE / SHOWING_CHOICES) keep input handling straightforward: the same key press does different things depending on state, so each branch stays small and testable.

tour.title: Game State Variables: GameStateVariableStorage.cs
tour.description: GameStateVariableStorage.cs connects the Yarn script variable system to the rest of the game. It extends the abstract `VariableStorageBehaviour` base class the YarnSpinner runtime requires, and for every `TryGetValue` / `SetValue` call it forwards to the GDScript `GameState` autoload via Godot `Call()` interop. This means a Yarn condition like `<<if $intro_complete>>` reads its value from the same place the rest of the game writes progression flags — there is no separate dialogue-only variable store.
tour.languageLesson: VariableStorageBehaviour is an abstract C# class that implements Godot's Node lifecycle and declares the full IVariableStorage interface. Extending it rather than implementing IVariableStorage directly gives GameStateVariableStorage automatic Godot node registration, inspector serialisation of declared variables, and save/load helpers — at the cost of committing to Godot's node tree for lifecycle management.

tour.title: Tests: Verifying the Dialogue System
tour.description: test_dialogue_box.gd and test_npc.gd are GUT unit test suites that pin down the two most testable layers of the system. test_dialogue_box.gd exercises every DialogueBox display mode (show_line, show_choices, typewriter lifecycle) and all emitted signals. test_npc.gd verifies that an NPC reads its yarn_node_id from Tiled metadata correctly, registers with CellRegistry, and gracefully handles an empty node ID without crashing.
tour.languageLesson: GUT (Godot Unit Test) tests extend the `GutTest` class and use `assert_eq`, `assert_true`, `assert_signal_emitted`, and similar assertion helpers. Because Godot objects are reference-counted nodes, GUT provides `add_child_autofree()` to ensure test subjects are freed between tests. The `await get_tree().process_frame` idiom advances Godot's frame loop inside a test, which is necessary to let Tweens and deferred calls fire before assertions run.
